subject: PPID zoning & exportability — procurement evidence request
messages:
From: Amy Cheng <amy@medixhealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com
Cc: procurement@medixhealth.com
Date: 2026-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: PPID zoning & exportability follow-up

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the demo last week — procurement asked me to consolidate a short list of evidence we need to complete our vendor onboarding and DPA annex negotiation. We have three priority asks for the legal/engineering review: 

1) A concise PII/PPID zoning map showing which fields are considered sensitive (PHI/SSN/email) and where those fields are stored/processed (transient cache, KV-store, long-term logs).
2) Confirmation of exportability: for customer-initiated data exports, is any plaintext PII included in the archive? If not, what pseudonymization/tokenization step is applied and where?
3) Subprocessor residency and export controls: a list of subprocessors that could touch exported data, their country locations, and whether transfers rely on SCCs/standard mechanisms.

Additionally, procurement wants to understand retention for exported archives (e.g., backup/forensics export storage) and if there is a KMS custody chain for archive keys. If you can provide a short timeline for the DPA annex redline + attestation artifacts, that would be very helpful — our final vendor board review is targeted for 09/10.

Can you send a PDF/Excel with the SSQ-style answers and a simple dataflow diagram? If a short call with your privacy engineer would help, we can make time next week.

Thanks,
Amy Cheng
Head of Procurement, MedixHealth
Amy.Cheng@medixhealth.com

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com
To: Amy Cheng <amy@medixhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, connor_obrien@redwood.example.com, kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
Date: 2026-08-29T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PPID zoning & exportability follow-up

Hi Amy — thanks for the clear list. Attaching an initial SSQ-style workbook (ssq_answers.xlsx) and an export/schema diagram (export-schema-diagram.png) that maps fields to storage/processing stages. High level answers below; please see attachments for the table-level mapping.

- Zoning: we mark fields at ingestion as PII/PPID using the classification pipeline. Pseudonymization (deterministic tokenization) is applied before long-term persistence for fields marked as PPID by default. Transient KV caches used by the inference runtime may contain raw inputs for up to 30 seconds; those caches are ephemeral and not written to durable logs.
- Exportability: exports initiated by customers are redacted by default for fields flagged PPID unless the customer opts into a full export. Redacted exports replace tokenized values with stable tokens; full exports include plaintext only if the account demonstrates lawful need and completes a separate export-approval workflow.
- Subprocessors & transfers: attached sheet includes subprocessors and locations. Transfers to non-EEA regions rely on SCCs where applicable; dedicated/private deployments can be provisioned to avoid cross-border transfers.

Proposed next steps:
1) Marissa (privacy eng) will add a short note on telemetry retention and logs.
2) Connor (legal) will propose a draft redline for the DPA annex and share the DocuSign link when ready.
3) If MedixHealth wants an attestation (KMS custody + SOC artifact), we can provide a scoped package within 7 business days.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call on Tuesday 08/31 10:00am PT?

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Sr. Product Counsel, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ssq_answers.xlsx (workbook), export-schema-diagram.png (image)

On Sun, Aug 29, 2026 at 11:02 AM lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com wrote:
> - Zoning: we mark fields at ingestion as PII/PPID using the classification pipeline.
> - Exportability: exports initiated by customers are redacted by default...

Hi Amy — quick technical addendum from the privacy engineering side: 

- Telemetry: inference telemetry is sampled and stripped of high-risk PII by the telemetry sanitization layer; fields that are classified PPID are hashed and replaced with stable tokens prior to telemetry export. Non-hashed debug traces are not shipped out of dedicated/private deployments.
- KV cache: the serving runtime holds KV cache in-GPU (or in-memory) and it is invalidated on model swap. There is no long-term persistence of KV cache in hosted mode.
- Export artifacts: customer export archive schema includes one logical CSV for "attributes" and one for "events"; the attributes CSV will only contain plaintext for fields where the export was explicitly approved by the customer. The export process generates a manifest.json that lists which fields were redacted/tokenized; we can provide a sample manifest.

I uploaded the full mapping + a sample manifest to our evidence folder: https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-ppid-evidence

Happy to join the call on Tue 08/31.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Privacy Engineer, Redwood Inference

2) Retention on exported archives: what's the default retention period if a customer does not explicitly set an export retention policy?

If you can drop the short answers into the workbook (ssq_answers.xlsx) and confirm the call time, we can finalize the vendor review schedule.

Best,
Amy

From: connor_obrien@redwood.example.com

Amy — answering your two clarifications and adding the legal timeline: 

1) Manifest flags: yes — manifest.json includes a per-field enum: ["plaintext", "tokenized", "redacted", "encrypted-at-rest"]. We will add a sample manifest row to the workbook showing the enum value for a representative attribute and an events row.
2) Default retention: exported archives created via the self-serve export tool default to 90 days retention in long-term object storage; customers can reduce this to as little as 7 days or extend it with a contractual amendment. Exports created as part of incident forensic packages are retained per the incident SLA (generally 180 days) unless otherwise requested.

Legal/DPA timeline: I uploaded a draft DPA annex redline to DocuSign and will share the envelope when it's ready for signature. We can provide a scoped KMS custody attestation within 7 business days after you accept the DPA redline; that package includes key custody diagrams and a chain-of-custody statement signed by our security lead.

Evidence drive: https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-ppid-evidence
